title: Cross-element refactoring and impact: rename, replace (repoint consumers), duplicate, move/reorder, delete with usages; transversal, per-role statuses live in the data.* and logic.* families

capabilities.title: Rename refactoring
capabilities.summary: `rename` refuses a name clash in the same scope and reports consumers and expressionsRewritten. Model references follow by key; free-typed literals are not rewritten.
capabilities.guidance: usages first, rename, then read each consumer back with get. On O11 fix `<Node>.<Output>` expressions by hand (set Value) after renaming a client action or its output (measured case); ODC rewrites them. A static entity record is renamed with set Identifier, not rename.

recommends.when: the element is an action: its per-role rename status
the element is a parameter or variable
the element is an entity, attribute or index

limits.text: Model references follow by key; literals, Description, CSS, button labels, index names and hand-written URLs keep the old name, and the consumer node keeps its own name.
A clash with a sibling name (an action, a structure attribute) is refused with the name the Studio would have used; a static entity record is renamed with set Identifier.
Renaming an exposed REST method rewrites its public URL; IEvent/ISystemEvent/IBlockEvent renames are refused or silently ignored.

differences: renaming a client action or its output rewrites the consumers' `<Node>.<Output>` expressions (O11 does not): jobs-odc rename-logic-propagation ops 82-90; renaming aggregate nodes rewrites their readers too: refactor-inherited ops 3-4

limits.text: After renaming a client action or its output parameter (the measured case), expressions that read `<Node>.<Output>` keep the old name (the consumer node itself is renamed): fix them with set Value, then Verify.
Renaming an exposed REST method rewrites the method segment of its URLPath (a renamed URL input its placeholder): outside callers break with no Verify message.

Model references follow by key; literals, Description, CSS, labels, index names and hand-written URLs keep the old name. A static entity record has no Name: rename writes its Identifier (the same write as set Identifier) and refuses a clash.

differences: `<Node>.<Output>` expressions are not rewritten after a client action or output rename (ODC rewrites them): jobs/rename-logic-propagation ops 82-88

capabilities.title: Repoint references (replace)
capabilities.summary: `replace from to` repoints each consumer of `from` to `to` by key (the Studio's ReplaceReferences), reporting rewired and stillPointingAtFrom; afterwards `from` has no consumers and `delete` needs no force. Same kind; a different kind needs force and usually breaks Verify; entities are refused.
capabilities.guidance: Give the destination the same signature first: children are not mapped, so inputs, outputs and attributes read by consumers must exist on it. Read usages on both sides afterwards. Entities cannot be repointed: rename, or move the consumers by hand.

recommends.when: the element is an action: create the destination with the same signature
the element is a static entity record

alternatives.when: the element keeps its identity and only its name must change

limits.text: Different kinds need force and usually break Verify; literals, descriptions, URLs and CSS never propagate.
Replace between entities is refused: their consumers bind to children (identifier type, attributes, anonymous record, list type) that ReplaceReferences does not map.
Replace between entities is refused: their consumers bind to children (identifier type, attributes, anonymous record, list type) that ReplaceReferences does not map.
Different kinds need force and usually break Verify; literals, descriptions, URLs and CSS never propagate.
limits.origin: api --op verbs: verbs.verbs.replace; kernel/AGENTS.md section 2 (replace); jobs/refactor-replace-action (description)

capabilities.title: Duplicate (Ctrl+D)
capabilities.summary: `duplicate` (Ctrl+D) makes a copy with the platform suffix (<Name>2) and no consumers; its content comes with it.
capabilities.guidance: Rename the copy afterwards (the suffix is the platform's). A copied action raises UnusedAction until something calls it: declare the warning or repoint a consumer with replace. An index is not duplicated: create another one with a different composition.

recommends.when: give the copy its final name
move the consumers of the original to the copy

limits.text: A duplicated action (and the actions of a duplicated screen) is UnusedAction until something calls it: declare the warning or repoint a consumer.
An index is refused: create another index with a different composition.
A copied action (and the actions of a copied screen) raise UnusedAction until called; the original keeps all its consumers.
An index is refused: create another index with a different composition.

capabilities.title: Sibling sequence
capabilities.summary: `move` reorders siblings of a sequence relative to a sibling, or sets x/y coordinates; with `into` it reparents: a top-level element changes folder and keeps its key; anything else goes through the Studio's own move, which gives a new key and rebinds every consumer (refused for public elements).
capabilities.guidance: Read the order back in the move result. To change parent create the object at the new parent and delete the old one. Children that are not an ordered sequence are refused and the message lists the sequences the parent has.

alternatives.when: a widget must change parent: a C# feature (IModelServices.MoveObject); the verb only reorders

requires.why: pending on O11 only: reparenting a widget needs a C# feature (the verb only reorders), and deliver.feature does not exist on O11 yet (on ODC it is an alternative)

limits.text: The verb only reorders: a sibling of another parent is refused (move only REORDERS inside the same parent).
Indexes and static entity records are not an ordered sequence: move is refused.

differences: index attributes are an ordered sequence: move is accepted (O11 refuses): jobs-odc/entity-refactor op 42

limits.text: Screen actions, indexes and static entity records have no author order: move is refused and the message lists the parent's sequences.
Index attributes are not reorderable: delete and recreate the index.

differences: index attributes are not an ordered sequence (ODC reorders them): jobs-negative/move-index-attribute

capabilities.title: Delete with usages
capabilities.summary: `delete` refuses while real consumers exist and names each one by path; derived usages (aggregate attribute lists, sample records) do not count. Run `usages` first, then repoint (replace) or rewrite each consumer; `force` breaks them (brokenConsumers) and is never the recommended path.

route.operation: {"op":"usages","target":"<path>"} then remove or replace each consumer, then {"op":"delete","target":"<path>"}

capabilities.guidance: Impact first: usages lists real and derived consumers. Remove leaf consumers first (expression, filter, call node, widget) or repoint them with replace, then delete without force (brokenConsumers 0). A forced delete was only observed (read back, integrity not verified).

recommends.when: the element is an action: per-role delete status
the element is an entity or attribute
a node in the middle of a flow: relink the predecessor first

alternatives.when: the consumers must keep working: repoint them to another element first

limits.text: Deleting sweeps down (children), never up: variables that only fed the deleted element stay as orphans. To delete a node in the middle of a flow relink the predecessor first.

An entity is refused because its generated `<Name> Record` cites it; a foreign key that binds to its identifier is not listed by usages. There is no clean path without force (observed: brokenConsumers counted, integrity not verified).
limits.origin: jobs-odc-negative/delete-entity-in-use; jobs-odc delete-entity-whole op 9, entity-refactor op 46

limits.text: An entity is refused even with no author consumer: its generated `<Name> Record` and `<Name> List` cite it; there is no clean path without force (observed with force: brokenConsumers counted, integrity not verified).
Deleting sweeps down, never up; the refusal lists consumer paths in an order that can change between runs.
